name: Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor
insider_take: This legendary colonial masterpiece has been the crown jewel of Siem Reap since 1932, where Charlie Chaplin once strolled and royalty still retreat.
whats_special: The hotel sits on the exact site where French explorer Henri Mouhot stayed in 1860 before "rediscovering" Angkor Wat. The original Art Deco facade remains untouched, and the famous Elephant Bar still serves the same Femme Fatale cocktail that captivated Somerset Maugham. Each suite features authentic Khmer artifacts and hand-carved furnishings by local artisans.
pro_tip: Book the Heritage Suite for exclusive access to the hotel's private collection of French colonial photographs and maps - some dating back to the 1920s temple excavations.
dont_miss: The hotel's secret underground tunnel that once connected to the Royal Palace, and the century-old frangipani tree in the courtyard where King Sihanouk held private audiences. Time your visit for the weekly traditional Apsara dance performance in the original ballroom.
pros: Historic colonial architecture with elegant French charm
Prime location minutes from Angkor Wat temple complex
Legendary Raffles service and hospitality standards
Beautiful tropical gardens and tranquil pool areas
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects heritage brand positioning
Historic building may have older room configurations
